NovaBio Therapeutics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

**Operator:**
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. [Standard operator instructions for Q&A participation.]

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

**Jordan Lee, VP of Investor Relations:**
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBio Therapeutics' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Lisa Wong, Chief Scientific Officer; Tom Reilly, Head of Commercial; and Karen Soto, Head of Manufacturing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO of NovaBio Therapeutics.

**Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:**
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. NovaBio Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust sales growth from our flagship immunology and oncology franchises, including NovaLume and Zoravax, alongside meaningful progress in our late-stage pipeline. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, with accelerated clinical enrollments, manufacturing scale-ups, and early market share gains in high-growth areas.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives, with a focus on our ramping R&D investments and pipeline priorities, updated revenue guidance and catalysts ahead, balance sheet and cash flow strength, strategies to navigate patent cliffs, disciplined operating expense management, core assumptions and risks, and exciting updates from our new product launches. We are particularly excited about Nova-ADC-301 and its potential to redefine treatment paradigms in HER2-positive solid tumors through superior linker technology and payload delivery.

Now, I will turn the call over to Sarah Chen, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

**Sarah Chen, CFO:**
Thank you, Elena. As Elena mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $4.85 billion, an increase of 26% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by 28% volume growth in NovaLume across U.S. and ex-U.S. markets, partially offset by modest pricing pressures from payer negotiations and the early impacts of the Inflation Reduction Act.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $1.45 billion, or $3.10 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $1.75 billion, or $3.75 per share.

Our operating expenses were $2.3 billion, reflecting continued heavy investment in R&D to advance our pipeline while capturing SG&A efficiencies from our field force optimization and digital tools. We continue to invest in R&D to support our pipeline. Our cash position remains strong at $6.2 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to revenue of $19.5 billion to $20.5 billion, non-GAAP EPS of $14.50 to $15.20, and R&D spend of $5.0 billion to $5.2 billion.

Let me expand on these results with more color across our key financial aspects, starting with our R&D expense and pipeline investment priorities, which remain the lifeblood of our long-term value creation in this dynamic biotech landscape. Q3 R&D expense came in at $1.28 billion, up 18% year-over-year from $1.09 billion in Q3 2023. For the nine months ended September 30th, we're at $3.72 billion, a 16% increase YoY. As a percentage of total revenue, R&D now stands at 27% on a trailing twelve-month basis—up from 23% last year—reflecting our deliberate acceleration into high-potential late-stage assets amid a favorable funding environment. This uptick was driven primarily by ramped-up manufacturing scale-up for our lead oncology ADC, ramped clinical trial enrollment across our immunology portfolio, and increased headcount in our computational biology group, now over 450 scientists leveraging AI-driven platforms.

Breaking this down by investment priorities, we've framed them around three pillars: oncology dominance at 52% of our R&D spend, or $665 million in Q3; immunology and inflammation at 28%, or $358 million; and emerging modalities in rare diseases and neuroscience at 20%, or $256 million. This allocation is informed by our risk-adjusted net present value models, targeting programs with peak sales potential exceeding $2 billion annually and probability of technical success above 40% in Phase 2 and beyond.

In oncology, we're laser-focused on antibody-drug conjugates, where we've seen category-leading success with peers like Daiichi Sankyo's Enhertu, which has reshaped HER2-positive breast cancer treatment. Our lead asset, Nova-ADC-301—a next-gen topoisomerase inhibitor ADC targeting solid tumors with a novel cleavable linker—absorbed 35% of our oncology spend this quarter. We're advancing it through a global Phase 3 trial in NSCLC and breast cancer, with topline data expected in H2 2025. Enrollment is ahead of schedule at 85% complete across 120 sites, thanks to our KOL network. We've also in-licensed a bispecific T-cell engager from a German biotech partner, investing $45 million in Q3 for Phase 1/2 initiation in hematologic malignancies—mirroring the momentum behind Amgen's tarlatamab in SCLC.

Shifting to immunology, 60% of this bucket went to our IL-23/IL-17 dual inhibitor, Nova-Inflam-45, now in Phase 3 for moderate-to-severe psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis. This program benefits from economies of scale similar to AbbVie's Skyrizi, with projected peak sales of $4.5 billion globally. We saw a 22% YoY increase here due to expanded combo trials with JAK inhibitors, addressing the post-JAK inhibitor safety concerns highlighted in recent FDA advisories.

Our emerging modalities pillar is where we're playing offense in next-gen tech. We've doubled down on gene editing and AAV-based therapies, allocating $150 million in Q3 to our CRISPR/Cas9 program for DMD—partnered with a Cambridge, MA-based outfit akin to CRISPR Therapeutics—following positive Phase 1/2 durability data showing 40% dystrophin expression at 12 months. In neuroscience, $60 million funded our ASO platform for ALS, inspired by Ionis' successes but with proprietary liver-targeting chemistry to minimize off-target effects.

On trends, we're bucking the industry-wide R&D efficiency crunch—pharma R&D productivity has flatlined at about one new approval per $2.6 billion spent, per Deloitte's latest benchmarks—by integrating AI/ML across discovery. Our AlphaFold-derived protein modeling has cut hit-to-lead timelines by 30%, saving an estimated $200 million annually. Externalization remains key: 42% of our pipeline is partnered or out-licensed, including a $500 million upfront deal with a major Chinese CRO for Asia-Pacific trials, yielding cost savings of 25-30% versus U.S. sites.

Regionally, U.S. operations command 55% of spend at $704 million, fueled by FDA fast-track designations on three assets and our Cambridge expansion. Europe, at 25% or $320 million, leverages EMA's PRIME scheme for our rare disease gene therapies, with key sites in the Netherlands and Switzerland. Asia-Pacific is growing fastest at 20% or $256 million, up 35% YoY, driven by China partnerships—think WuXi AppTec-style CMC manufacturing—which de-risk trial execution amid U.S.-China tensions and expedite market entry into the world's second-largest pharma market, valued at $170 billion.

Strategically, these investments position us for a $15 billion revenue inflection by 2030, with 12 Phase 3 readouts and five potential approvals over the next 24 months. We're maintaining discipline: our R&D-to-sales ratio is projected to peak at 28% in FY24 before tapering to 22% by FY27 as royalties and milestones kick in. Burn rate is controlled at $4.1 billion annually, fully funded through 2027 with our $6.2 billion in cash and undrawn facilities. Looking ahead, FY24 R&D guidance is $5.0-$5.2 billion, implying 14-17% growth. Q4 will see stepped-up spend on Nova-ADC-301 commercial readiness and neuroscience IND filings. We're excited about the derisked path ahead in this era of precision medicine, where oncology and immunology continue to drive 70% of the $1.5 trillion global pharma market growth through 2030, per IQVIA.

Turning now to our revenue guidance and key upcoming catalysts that position NovaBio for sustained growth. NovaBio is a fully integrated biopharma leader with a diversified portfolio spanning oncology, immunology, and rare diseases, anchored by our flagship PD-1 inhibitor, NovaLume—similar to Keytruda in mechanism but with enhanced bispecific antibody engineering for better tumor penetration—which continues to drive the lion's share of our topline.

Q3 net product revenues came in strong at $4.85 billion, up 26% year-over-year, fueled by NovaLume's U.S. volumes growing 18% YoY despite headwinds from the IRA's price negotiation framework. Ex-U.S. sales surged 42% YoY, driven by strong launches in Japan and emerging markets like Brazil and India, where we've secured favorable reimbursement in 15 additional countries. Gross-to-net adjustments held steady at 22%, better than guided due to optimized patient assistance programs and 340B contract optimizations.

We're raising our full-year 2024 revenue outlook to $19.5 billion to $20.5 billion, implying 24% to 29% YoY growth at the midpoint. Oncology remains our growth engine at 62% of projected revenues, led by NovaLume's contribution on track for peak sales exceeding $6 billion by 2028, incorporating label expansions into MSI-high endometrial cancers. Immunology at 25% benefits from NovaFlex's stability and the ramp-up of NovaDerm, which captured 12% share in psoriasis. Rare diseases round out at 13%, with NovaGene-X for SMA hitting 95% market penetration in eligible pediatric patients.

Regionally, U.S. sales guided to 70% of total, with net pricing stable despite IRA risks; Europe and Canada up 35% YoY; ex-China International growing 50% via Takeda and Zydus partnerships; China pending CFDA approval for NovaLume. Non-GAAP EPS guidance narrowed to $14.50 to $15.20, supported by gross margins expanding through manufacturing scale-up.

Key upcoming catalysts include topline Phase 3 data for NovaLume plus ADC combo in HER2-low breast cancer in Q4 2024 from NOVALUME-301, with positive PFS potentially supporting BLA in H1 2025 targeting $4 billion TAM. FDA PDUFA for NovaDerm in Crohn's on January 15, 2025, adding $3 billion TAM. Interim data from NovaGene-Y CAR-T in solid tumors at ASH 2024. Strategic M&A with $1.5 billion allocated, including a Phase 2 oral GLP-1/GIP agonist. Ex-U.S. milestones like Japan PMDA for NovaLume and EMA for NovaTox-ADX. These align with our '3-3-3' framework and collectively offer over $15 billion in risk-adjusted NPV.

Next, our cash flow and balance sheet highlights underscore the strength and flexibility of our position. As of September 30th, we ended with cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaling $6.2 billion, up 18% sequentially and 32% YoY. Net cash at $3.6 billion after $2.6 billion in long-term debt at 3.8% blended rate. Leverage at 0.4x net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA, with DSO at 52 days, inventory at 4.2 months, and intangibles at $5.4 billion including $450 million from CRISPR licensing.

Operating cash flow hit $925 million, 105% of adjusted EBITDA, from high-margin product revenues and AI revenue cycle management. Free cash flow at $685 million after capex for CAR-T facilities. Financing included $400 million share repurchases and $75 million dividends. FY24 FCF guidance $2.6-2.8 billion provides 24 months runway.

On patent cliff exposure and lifecycle management strategies, our exposure is manageable at 28% of revenue from products like Zoravax expiring Q4 2027 U.S., mitigated to project 55-65% post-cliff retention. Strategies include label expansions adding $450 million revenue, formulation innovations like Zoravax-XR at 22% share, companion diagnostics with Roche, next-gen pipeline like Zoravax-2 entering Phase 3, and regional hedging with local JVs. Lifecycle NPV exceeds $12 billion.

For operating expense analysis, total OpEx was $2.3 billion, up 14% YoY but flat sequentially adjusted, at 47% of revenue. R&D at $1.28 billion or 56%, driven by Phase 3 trials and AI efficiencies; SG&A at $900 million up 4%, with commercial ramps offset by ERP savings. Regional mix U.S.-heavy. FY24 OpEx guidance $8.5-8.8 billion implies margin expansion.

Key assumptions include 65% PTS for NBX-101 ADC, 18% volume growth, stable pricing, 20% AI productivity gains, and macro stability yielding EPS $14.50-$15.20. Risks encompass clinical failures (30-50% prob), reimbursement pressures (40%), supply chain issues (25%), competition, and macro factors; downside -15% revenue.

Finally, new product launch updates: NOV-ADC-301 sales $285 million Q3, 18% U.S. NRx share in HER2 mBC, eroding Kadcyla; NOV-ADC-402 pre-launch traction. Q4 sales $350-380 million, raised FY guidance $1.05-1.15 billion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Raj Patel, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

**Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer:**
Thank you, Sarah. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, Nova-ADC-301 Phase 3 enrollment at 85% with H2 2025 data; Nova-Inflam-45 Phase 3 advancing in psoriasis; CRISPR DMD Phase 1/2 positive; ASO ALS platform funded. Upcoming milestones include NOVALUME-301 PFS readout Q4 2024, NovaDerm PDUFA Jan 2025, CAR-T ASH data. We expect to file multiple BLAs in 2025.

Next, Dr. Lisa Wong will provide an update on our research pipeline.

**Dr. Lisa Wong, Chief Scientific Officer:**
Thank you, Raj. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research. Advancements include AI/ML integration cutting timelines 30%, AlphaFold modeling, bispecific engager in-licensing, gene editing with 40% dystrophin expression, and ASO neuroscience with off-target minimization. Our externalization strategy with 42% partnered pipeline de-risks execution.

Now I'll turn the call over to Tom Reilly, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

**Tom Reilly, Head of Commercial:**
Thank you, Lisa. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with NovaLume up 18% volumes, NovaDerm 12% psoriasis share, NOV-ADC-301 18% NRx in HER2 space. We're seeing strong uptake in oncology and immunology segments across U.S. (70% mix), Europe, and Asia. Our marketing campaigns are proving effective in driving formulary wins, KOL engagement, and 92% gross-to-net retention amid IRA headwinds.

Finally, Karen Soto will discuss our manufacturing operations.

**Karen Soto, Head of Manufacturing:**
Thank you, Tom. Our manufacturing operations are running smoothly. We've scaled Singapore facility to 120,000 vials/month for ADCs, cut COGS to 22%, locked 85% 2025 API costs, and invested in CAR-T fill-finish in North Carolina for 2025 qualification. Supply chain updates include WuXi partnerships for 25-30% savings and just-in-time biologics inventory. We are focused on CMC readiness for five Phase 3 assets and viral vector expansion to 5,000L.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Elena.

**Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:**
Thank you, Karen. We will now open the call for questions.

**Operator:**
[Operator instructions.] Our first question comes from Jane Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

**Jane Doe, Goldman Sachs:**
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Can you elaborate on the R&D allocation shift toward oncology ADCs and how that impacts FY25 priorities?

**Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:**
Thanks, Jane. Oncology at 52% reflects high rNPV programs like Nova-ADC-301, with 35% spend there and enrollment ahead. FY25 will balance with immunology ramps, maintaining 14-17% growth while AI efficiencies save $200 million.

**Operator:**
Our next question comes from Mike Rivera with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

**Mike Rivera, Morgan Stanley:**
Great, thanks. On the raised revenue guidance, what gives you confidence amid IRA risks, and details on China catalysts?

**Sarah Chen, CFO:**
Mike, confidence stems from NovaLume volumes and ex-U.S. 42% surge, with guidance midpoint 26% growth. China CFDA for NovaLume by year-end unlocks $300 million peak, modeled conservatively at $0-50 million this year.

**Operator:**
Our next question comes from Lisa Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

**Lisa Kim, JPMorgan:**
Thanks. For clinical risks on NBX-101 and gene therapies, how do PTS assumptions hold up?

**Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer:**
Lisa, our 65% PTS for NBX-101 is conservative vs. 55% ADC benchmark, backed by TROJAN platform's 78% preclinical hit rate. Gene therapies at 75% enrollment leverage Lonza scale-up; diversified 12 Phase 2+ assets mitigate.

**Operator:**
Our next question comes from Alex Thompson with Barclays. Please go ahead.

**Alex Thompson, Barclays:**
Appreciate it. Impressive NOV-ADC-301 share gains—sustainability vs. Kadcyla biosimilars?

**Tom Reilly, Head of Commercial:**
Alex, 18% NRx driven by superior ORR/PFS data, 85% formulary coverage, and $250 million DTC campaign. Premium profile sustains vs. Kadcyla cliff, projecting 22% year-end share.

**Operator:**
Our next question from David Lee with BofA Securities.

**David Lee, BofA Securities:**
On patent cliffs, how do lifecycle strategies offset Zoravax erosion?

**Sarah Chen, CFO:**
David, multi-pronged approach—expansions, XR formulations at 22% share, next-gen bispecifics—delivers $1.2 billion incremental revenue, 55-65% retention, $12 billion NPV.

**Operator:**
That concludes questions at this time.

**Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:**
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

**Jordan Lee, VP of Investor Relations:**
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

**Operator:**
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
